geography: Worldwide (combined ex-US Onbrez Breezhaler and US Arcapta Neohaler line; no split printed)
revenue_scope: Worldwide net sales of Novartis's combined indacaterol product line as printed in its interim report product table: row 'Onbrez Breezhaler' until Q4 2011 (and Q1 2010 narrative), 'Arcapta Neohaler/Onbrez Breezhaler' or 'Onbrez Breezhaler/Arcapta Neohaler' from Q1 2012. Not a US-only Arcapta Neohaler line; Novartis prints no US/ex-US split.

approval_evidence.quote: NDA 022383/Orig-01 NDA APPROVAL Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation ... for Arcapta Neohaler (indacaterol maleate inhalation powder), 75 mcg

series_start_reason: First quarter Novartis prints the indacaterol line. The Q4 2009 report (0001104659-10-002886) prints no sales figure, so 2009Q4 (1) is the prior-year cell of the Q4 2010 report (0001370368-11-000003); no earlier quarter is printed. launch_quarter is null because the Onbrez Breezhaler launch in Germany (December 2009, see notes) is the ex-US brand, not the Arcapta Neohaler named in drug_name, which FDA approved in 2011.
series_end_reason: Novartis out-licensed US commercialization of its COPD portfolio to Sunovion: the Q2 2017 report (0001370368-17-000062) states 'In the US, Sunovion Pharmaceuticals Inc. has assumed as of December 21, 2016 US commercialization rights for Utibron Neohaler, Arcapta Neohaler and Seebri Neohaler. Novartis will continue to bring Ultibro Breezhaler, Onbrez Breezhaler and Seebri Breezhaler to patients with COPD outside of the US.' From 2017Q1 the Novartis row is therefore ex-US and a different scope, so the worldwide series ends at 2016Q4. Novartis also stopped printing the three brand rows after the Q4 2019 report, replacing them from Q1 2020 (0001370368-20-000061) with a combined 'Ultibro Group' row.
notes: Judgement call: the only Novartis figure for this product is the combined indacaterol line, so the series is that line and not a US-brand-only measure. Launch of the ex-US brand: Onbrez Breezhaler received European approval in November 2009 and was launched in Germany in December 2009 (Q4 2009 report, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1114448/000110465910002886/a10-2460_16k.htm: 'gained European regulatory approval in November 2009 as Onbrez Breezhaler and was launched in Germany in December'). The US brand Arcapta Neohaler was FDA-approved in 2011 (Q2 2011 report, 0001370368-11-000021, reports the US approval in July 2011); no Novartis document read dates its US launch. The row label is 'Onbrez Breezhaler' through Q4 2011 and names Arcapta Neohaler from Q1 2012 (0001370368-12-000024); the figures are one continuous printed line and the Q4 2016 report text pairs the names ('Onbrez Breezhaler/Arcapta Neohaler (USD 36 million)'). Rows for 2017Q1 to 2019Q4 exist but are ex-US (see series_end_reason) and are not used. 2010Q1 (3) is derived from the Q2 2010 report's table row 'Onbrez' (six months 8 less Q2 5); the Q1 2010 report's own narrative prints the same 3 ('Onbrez Breezhaler (QAB149) (USD 3 million)', no table row), while the Q1 2011 report's prior-year cell prints 2, which is not used because it disagrees with the six-month figure 8 and the 2010 full year 33 = 3+5+8+17. The Q2 2010 and Q3 2010 table rows are labelled 'Onbrez'. Four quarters sum to the full years printed in the Q4 reports: 2010 33, 2011 103, 2012 134, 2013 192, 2014 220, 2015 166, 2016 143; 2009 is 1.
search_log: Listed all Novartis (CIK 1114448) filings via data.sec.gov submissions (all forms, current and older pages, not filtered to one form). Downloaded the quarterly interim financial report exhibit of every results 6-K from 2010Q2 to 2026Q2 (EX-99.2 / a*-99_2.htm, or the 6-K body for 2010) and parsed every HTML table by script, taking the row whose first cell is the brand label in the table whose header begins with the quarter (Qn YYYY).

Bigdata.com was used to locate documents; every cited URL is the sec.gov Archives original. Compared each quarter's own value with the prior-year column of the same quarter one year later and with the printed full-year totals; differences are named in notes.

Looked for a US partner or licensee that prints the brand's own sales (rung c): Sunovion (Sumitomo Pharma) assumed US commercialization rights as of 2016-12-21 per the Novartis Q2 2017 report; a Bigdata.com search of Sumitomo Pharma filings for Utibron, Seebri and Arcapta Neohaler returned no result and no Sumitomo document was obtained, so no US-only line is used.

Q4 2009 report (0001104659-10-002886) and Q1 2010 report (0001104659-10-020578) downloaded and searched for Onbrez: Q4 2009 gives the December 2009 German launch with no sales figure; Q1 2010 gives 'Onbrez Breezhaler (QAB149) (USD 3 million)'.

Rung c re-tried after review: Sumitomo Pharma (owner of Sunovion) supplementary financial data ebr20170511.2 to ebr20200130.2 (pdfplumber grep for utibron|seebri|arcapta): the North America sales table carries one line 'Therapeutic agent for COPD (in-licensed 3 products)' / 'New products for COPD' covering Utibron, Seebri and Arcapta together, so no Arcapta-only figure and nothing usable beyond the Novartis line. Sunovion is not an SEC filer.
